A race pace says where it came from · #674

Chosen: Fasettrun 19 criteria held12 decisions4 one-way doorsrisk: ageing turns a converted point into a bandunattended: one variant

Fasett: the ≈ 4:10 /km facet is what you tap. In the session header, the number after Mål 10 km-fart has a dotted underline and opens one small popover. In a done session's Token Sentence, the chip opens it. In a planned session, the chip still opens the editor, and the editor's last line becomes this provenance. A pointer opens the same popover on hover (300 ms) or keyboard focus; a planned chip shows a one-line tooltip on hover. The popover gives the pace, how it was reached (Fra / Omregnet fra 5 km-resultatet ditt 3. mai), the source time and whether it was typed or measured, with the device credit in #670's words, and the confidence as a word, three bars and the reason. It also carries the derived Garmin/Polar credit and a link to Løpsresultater. When anything on the page is derived from Garmin or Polar data, that credit also stays visible under the stanza.

VariantFasett Chosen
Axis positionInteraction model: the line opens from the number it explains (not always visible, not a sheet, not a separate info icon)
GainNo new chrome on a dense line. The question "where does 4:10 come from?" is asked by touching 4:10. One body serves the header, a done chip and the editor's closing line, so the three can never disagree.
CostA planned chip's tap is already taken by the editor, so there the line sits one tap deep (in the editor) and a pointer gets a tooltip. The header facet becomes a second interactive element in a line that has none today.

Worst caseA 51-character Garmin device and "Polar Grit X2 Pro Titan" wrap under the icon. 95–105 % maratonfart ≈ 6:01–6:39 /km fits on the header line at 390 px and wraps whole at 320 px. At 320 px the popover flips above or scrolls inside itself. No horizontal overflow at 320, 390 or 1440 px. No console errors.

StatusChosen

Decisions

  • Where does the line open? From the ≈ number in the session header, from a done session's chip, and as the closing line of a planned chip's editor. A pointer gets hover and focus on the first two and a tooltip on the third. po, two-way.
  • What does it say? Pace; Fra or Omregnet fra <distanse>-resultatet ditt <dato>, with the year only when it differs; the time and skrevet inn av deg or målt av klokka · Garmin Forerunner 265, matching #670; Høy/Middels/Lav sikkerhet: <the weakest signal>, and for a low conversion "Derfor et spenn, ikke én fart"; then a link to Løpsresultater. po, two-way.
  • Where does the derived Garmin/Polar credit go? In the popover, and always visible as SourceCredits under the stanza, because house rule says a credit is never only in a tooltip or a fold (source-credits.tsx, ADR 0098 §3). dev, one-way: applies ADR 0098 to plan-side targets resolved from measured results.
  • Does ageing move Planned TSS? No. The resolution's point is always the model's exponent (1.06). The low band is display only, so Planned TSS stays a function of results alone (criteria 7 and 8). Settled by probe: a 20:00 5 km viewed on 20 Nov 2027 turns 10 km-fart into ≈ 4:10–4:26 /km, and its fast edge never moves. dev, one-way: what Planned TSS is computed from.
  • Two distances tie on ratio? The newer result wins, then the longer distance. Probe: for 10 km-fart, a 5 km and a 20 km run on the same day pick the 20 km. dev, two-way.
  • Same anchor, same day, typed and measured? The typed one wins, as #670 decided. Probe: the worst-case 7,5 km pair picks the typed result. dev, two-way.
  • Pace format. The app's own 4:10 /km (formatPace, boundedRange), not the issue's shorthand 4:10/km. Not a decision; noted.
  • Løpsresultater intro. It says sessions use "ditt nyeste resultat på den distansen". Amend it: "…eller, uten et, omregnet fra resultatet nærmest i distanse". po, two-way.
  • I dag row. It shows ≈ 4:10 /km and gets no line (tapping the row opens the session). If the pace was derived from a Garmin/Polar result, it carries the derived credit in the row's existing credit slot. dev, one-way (ADR 0098 §6); architecture to confirm.
  • Facet and done-chip tap target? An invisible after: hit area to about 44 px. Critic, dev, two-way.
  • Which popover? The existing TokenPopover handle (trap-focus, retargeting) for the facet, done chips and the editor footer, with a 500 ms hover delay. Critic, dev, two-way.
  • A Planned TSS read from a Garmin or Polar result, on the MCP? It binds to that result's Origin Platform (ADR 0098 §2): Polar closes model without the opt-in, and Garmin carries its credit. Critic, dev, one-way: what the MCP sends. Architecture to confirm.

Critic's scoring

1 Name ≈ pace, 20:00 5 km → 10 km-fart ≈ 4:10holds: header and popover; the chip stays name-only, as today
2 Nearest by ratio, newest, off-anchor counts, at-anchor winsholds: 15 km → HM; 10 km Garmin is rung 1; the tie goes to the newer, then the longer
3 Weakest of ratio and ageholds: 5→10 Middels by age; 5→HM Lav by ratio; day 90 is medium

6 Garmin/Polar creditholds on screen: popover, plus SourceCredits visible while closed; the model binding is decision C

9 At-anchor athletes unchanged, now with a lineholds: 41:30 → 4:09, as today

Craft: the motion matches motion-popup and motion-tooltip. A 300 ms hover open on a meta line the pointer crosses fires popovers nobody asked for, so the delay should be 500 ms. A done chip opens a popover on hover while a planned chip that looks the same opens a tooltip; that holds because both use the same words. Fit: this is the glossary's "the number is the facet" rule, and the next ticket's "what would fix it" line uses the same body on a dashed chip. Full critique: evidence:critic.md. Probes: critic-probe/.

Designer's pick

Fasett, the same as the critic's. One tension: the designer opens on hover after 300 ms on a new Base UI Popover; the critic would use 500 ms on the existing TokenPopover handle so Tab reaches the link and the chips retarget.

Method

Emil's prototype (bredvid-design-engineering prototype-ui), standalone branch: prototype.html in the app's tokens, a picker with one variant, a Demo/Worst case toggle and harness controls for results, viewing day, planned/done and theme. The ladder is computed live: rung 1 picks the newest result, a typed result wins on the same day, then the nearest distance by ratio; Riegel 1.06; a low conversion gets a 1.06–1.15 band, with a percentage applied to both edges. Probe (probe/probe.mjs, Playwright from the repo): 10 km-fart ≈ 4:10 /km and halvmaratonfart ≈ 4:22–4:58 /km from a 20:00 5 km, matching the criteria; 105 % maratonfart ≈ 4:20–5:15 /km. Checked: hover, leave, focus and Esc; reduced motion (no scale); no overflow and the popover inside the viewport at 320/390/1440.

Code it touches

app/utils/zones/resolve.ts (racePace arm, RaceAnchorPaces becomes results + provenance), app/utils/intensity-target.ts (describeStepTarget, formatIntensityTarget, sessionMetricTarget), app/utils/workout-notation.ts (intensityToken facets carry the provenance), app/components/score-stanza.tsx (the chip becomes a trigger on read-only surfaces), app/routes/training/sessions.$sessionId.tsx (header facet, SourceCredits under the stanza), app/routes/training/__intensity-popover.tsx + app/utils/zone-equivalent.ts (closing line for racePace), app/utils/source-attribution.ts (derivedAttributionLines), app/utils/load/planned-tss.server.ts, app/utils/labels/token-editor.ts, labels/meg.ts, new equivalence-model reference data (ADR 0006 pattern).

Rejected directions

  • Always-visible line under each step: four lines of provenance on a four-line stanza; the Score's density is the point.
  • An ⓘ icon beside the chip: adds a second chip-like mark to the line (§7.2: the chip is the line's only chip-shaped element).
  • A bottom sheet: too heavy for a sentence of provenance; fine pointer users lose hover.

Fasett Chosen

Working prototype below. Pick results, the viewing day and planned/done in the harness. Tap the ≈ number or a chip.

Worst case

Critic (break-ui): Fragile: a Planned TSS read from a Polar result would reach model without the opt-in, because plannedReading binds only the Workout's set (decision C). Ugly: the facet's tap target is 18 px. Fragile: 200 % zoom at 320 px was not checked; it needs max-height: var(--available-height). Held: long devices, a whole band wrapping at 320 px, ties, the Feb 29 date, no results, dark mode, and no overflow.

Found by the worst case: (1) at 320 px the editor plus the provenance runs past the viewport, so the popover must use collision avoidance with internal scroll, as Base UI does; fixed in the prototype. (2) The Garmin derived credit is English and hyphenates "device-sourced" mid-word; it is quoted text, so leave it. (3) A band on a percentage range (95–105 %) reads as a range of a range; the label stays authored and the band is one span, which holds.
